title: Introduce operator quiesce and safe rollback to reduce tenant impact during on-prem upgrades
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Several customers reported tenant-facing outages during recent on-prem operator upgrades. Symptoms include long-running helm post-upgrade hooks timing out, operator leader-election churn, and simultaneous reconciles that produced duplicate CRs and transient configmap/KV schema mismatches. Impacted tenants saw serving pods crashloop or lose affinity to their persisted KV caches, triggering expensive rollback/replay flows and customer escalations. Root cause analysis points to a race between helm post-upgrade hooks + external-secret rotation and the operator's reconcile loop: the operator would attempt to reconcile while cluster resources were in a transient state, create or reapply resources, and then helm's garbage collection would compete, leaving the tenant in partial state. This ticket implements a coordinated "quiesce" mode (temporarily pause non-essential reconciles for affected tenant namespaces during upgrade windows) and a safe automatic rollback orchestrator to return tenants to the last-consistent manifest when an upgrade enters a degraded state.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy current on-prem operator vX.Y to a test tenant with external-secrets enabled
2) Trigger helm upgrade that includes CRD and mutatingwebhook changes and rotate external secret simultaneously
3) Observe timeout on helm post-upgrade hook after 2m, operator leader election churns (multiple leaders within 60s), and reconciles happen while helm apply is incomplete
4) Validate that duplicate CRs or partial updates to ConfigMap/KV cache appear and that tenant application pods restart or report config-schema-errors
mitigation_actions: Applied emergency guard in operator to detect active helm upgrade annotations and deprioritize reconcilers for affected namespaces (short-term patch deployed to on-prem customers SUP-2104)
Added temporary alert (pager) on helm-posthook-duration > 90s and operator-leader-change > 3 in 2m to escalate earlier
Provided customers a manual quiesce command (kubectl annotate tenant/quiesce=true) as an immediate workaround while we ship the coordinated feature
proposed_fix_summary: Implement a tenant-scoped quiesce mode in the operator: when an upgrade window is detected (via helm annotations or operator API), the operator will pause reconcilers that mutate tenant resources except for heartbeat/health controllers. Introduce an automated rollback orchestrator: on detecting repeated reconcile errors or failed helm post-hooks, record the previous stable manifest snapshot and rollback tenant resources in a controlled order (CRDs -> namespaced resources -> secrets) with rate-limited operations and post-rollback validation checks.
acceptance_criteria: Quiesce mode can be enabled via annotation or operator API and prevents non-essential mutating reconciles for a namespace
Automated rollback orchestrator reverts a failed upgrade to the last stable manifest and validates tenant application readiness within the SLA window
New unit and e2e tests that simulate helm post-upgrade timeouts, external-secret rotation, and operator leader churn pass consistently in CI
Deployable hotfix PR merged and can be rolled out to consenting on-prem customers with a documented runbook
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR with quiesce + rollback feature behind feature-flag (operator repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/2876)
2) Run Canary on internal test clusters and one low-risk customer (72h observation)
3) Iterate based on telemetry and enable gradual rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% of consenting on-prem tenants
4) Ship post-release runbook and automation to opt-in customers and update upgrade preflight checks
monitoring_and_metrics: Track helm-posthook-duration (histogram) and percent of upgrades exceeding 90s
Percent of upgrades that trigger automated rollback and time-to-restore (p95)
postmortem_notes: Initial incident created from multiple customer escalations on 2025-03-07; primary signal was support ticket SUP-2104 and Slack escalation #cust-escalations
Root cause is a coordination gap between helm upgrade hooks, external-secret rotations, and operator reconcile ordering under leader-election flapping
Long-term prevention: strengthen preflight checks, surface upgrade windows in operator, and avoid cross-system simultaneous rotations where possible
Follow-ups: update docs for recommended upgrade choreography and add CI scenario that simulates slow kube-apiserver responses
